finding: WA Health's Chief Health Officer guideline for hairdressing is issued under the Public Health Act 2016. finding: The guideline's section 13.1 covers mobile operators. They must have hand-washing facilities with warm water, soap and paper towels, a suitable treatment area, equipment cleaning between clients, a sharps container, and wastewater discharged to sewer rather than stormwater.
source_name: WA Health - Guideline for the hairdressing industry (Chief Health Officer guideline under Public Health Act 2016)

finding: The guideline says home-based operators must meet the same requirements as salon operators, and must contact their local government before operating to discuss planning and building approvals.
source_name: WA Health - Guideline for the hairdressing industry (Chief Health Officer guideline under Public Health Act 2016)

finding: The guideline says dye mixing bowls must be cleaned after each use, and food preparation must not occur where dyes are mixed. Bleach is mentioned only as an option for disinfecting hard-to-clean surfaces after a detergent clean. Blood-contaminated equipment is cleaned first, then immersed in 70 per cent alcohol or a hospital-grade disinfectant, and products are labelled with name, date and dilution.
source_name: WA Health - Guideline for the hairdressing industry (Chief Health Officer guideline under Public Health Act 2016)
notes: Product-specific rules for colour and bleach beyond these points not found.

finding: The guideline does not require formal health screening of staff or clients. For clients with an open wound, infection or skin condition, the guideline advises recommending a GP visit first. It says head lice do not prevent a client attending.
